To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the brain generates electrical signals when it is engaged in remembering specific experiences and in the awareness of remembering; 2) these signals are generated by networks of brain cells that are specialized for the storage and retrieval functions of memory; and 3) these signals provide information about how the brain stores and retrieves facts and experiences.

1) The electrical signals of the human brain are altered during the retrieval of memories for specific facts or episodes; 2) The electrical changes that accompany retrieval can be used to distinguish memories that are accurate from memories that are inaccurate; 3) The electrical changes associated with retrieval can be used as a marker for the conscious experience of remembering.

(a) electrical signals in the brain are associated with the learning and remembering of factual information and of specific experiences from the human past, and (b) these signals reflect the storage of memories within the brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the brain represents and remembers facts and experiences.
the brain mechanisms of memory and awareness.
how the brain represents and stores information, how this information is accessed and manipulated, and what the subjective experience is when this information is accessed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
electrical signals of the brain can be used to study the neural mechanisms of memory and of the awareness of remembering.
the electrical signals of memory and of the awareness of remembering are the result of the interaction of the brain with the environment and are not a direct reflection of the memory itself.
the brain's electrical signals provide a window on the workings of memory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
memory is a complex, dynamic, distributed process, and that electrical signals in the brain can be used to identify the different components and stages of the memory system.
electrical signals in the brain are associated with memory and awareness of remembering.
electrical signals in the brain can reveal how information is stored and retrieved, and that these signals can provide insight into the nature of the conscious experience of remembering.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electrical signals can be used to study the brain in action.
the brain’s activity is a reflection of the mind’s work, and that electrical signals in the brain can be used to investigate mental processes and to develop better treatments for memory disorders.
memory and awareness are two sides of a coin, and that the electrical signals of memory and awareness can be dissociated from each other.
